conflicts.name: Overlapping scopes
conflicts.description: Two attempts with overlapping path scopes provision independent worktrees and indices. Neither attempt can observe or mutate the other's worktree, index, or policy context. The scope fence keeps each attempt's writes inside its own owned paths.
assertions: Each attempt provisions a distinct worktree with a detached HEAD at the baseline oid
A file written in attempt A's worktree is not visible in attempt B's worktree
The caller repository's index and HEAD are unchanged after both attempts provision
Each attempt's policy context path is distinct and not shared

conflicts.name: Competing owners
conflicts.description: Two OS processes acquire the same attempt's ownership concurrently. SQLite WAL serializes the acquisition; exactly one wins and the other receives RICKGENT_STATE_CONFLICT. No partial reservation (credential without resources, or resources without credential) is left behind.
assertions: Exactly one of the two competing workers acquires ownership; the other receives RICKGENT_STATE_CONFLICT
The durable ownership lease table has exactly one row for the attempt after the race
The durable resource claim table has exactly 11 rows (the fixed resource set) for the attempt after the race
No partial reservation (credential row without resource rows) is persisted

conflicts.name: Foreign commits
conflicts.description: An attempt cannot claim another attempt's commit or release its lease. A worker with attempt A's ownership cannot finalize cleanup using attempt B's attempt-ref oid, and cannot observe or mutate attempt B's commit attribution or cleanup artifacts.
assertions: A worker with attempt A ownership cannot update attempt B's attempt ref to a foreign oid without corrupting B's durable baseline (the store's cleanup validation rejects a foreign attempt ref oid)
Attempt A's ownership lease is bound to attempt A's attempt id; attempt B's lease is bound to attempt B's attempt id
Attempt A's commit attribution (if any) is not observable as attempt B's commit attribution
A foreign ownership grant (attempt A's grant presented for attempt B) is rejected by isAuthorizedAttemptOwnershipGrant / assertFresh

Unauthorized ref movement is detected and rejected by the production authority path (provisionAttemptWorkspace/assertRef → containFailure → LeaseAuthority.beginCleanup); the rival's ownership is transitioned to cleanup_pending and the durable baseline is unchanged (the foreign oid does not persist as the rival's authoritative ref)

No commit attribution row is persisted for the rival attempt after the foreign ref write (the authority mint capability is held by LeaseAuthority; the ownership plan binds the attemptRef to the owning attempt)
The authority path constrains commits to the owning attempt: attempt A's provisioned attemptRef is bound to attempt A's ref, not attempt B's ref
No test-code rollback: the production authority path (not test/worker code) detects and rejects the unauthorized ref movement

conflicts.name: Delivery-ref movement
conflicts.description: One attempt's cleanup moves the run's delivery ref while another attempt is in flight. The in-flight attempt's baseline oid is preserved in the durable store and is not corrupted by the delivery-ref movement. No attempt can release another attempt's lease during delivery-ref movement.
assertions: The delivery ref movement (git update-ref) does not change the in-flight attempt's durable delivery_baseline_oid
The in-flight attempt's attempt ref is not moved by the delivery-ref movement
The in-flight attempt's worktree HEAD remains at its baseline oid
The delivery ref movement does not release or alter the in-flight attempt's ownership lease

conflicts.name: Stubborn descendants
conflicts.description: A worker spawns a stubborn descendant process tree (double-fork escape attempt) through the ProcessSupervisor so the process tree is observed and reaped. The detached grandchild is explicitly killed and verified dead. The descendant cannot escape the attempt's containment: no sentinel file appears outside the attempt's owned output directory, and the descendant process is reaped before the attempt's ownership is released.
assertions: A double-fork escape attempt does not create a marker file outside the attempt's owned output directory
The production Docker containment backend observes and reaps the process tree via cgroup.kill (the authority-owned terminate-all); a durable launch/boundary id is persisted

The authority-owned death receipt confirms all-descendant death (descendantsConfirmedDead=true, proofBasis=authoritative_containment, emptinessConfirmed=true); a missing emptiness confirmation fails closed
No direct process.kill on an untrusted PID is used; the production containment backend reaps all descendants (not a survivor PID from a report file)
A missing survivor report is NOT treated as success (fail closed); the containment backend's emptiness confirmation is the authority
The rival attempt's output directory is not mutated by the stubborn descendant

conflicts.name: Output floods
conflicts.description: A worker floods its stdout and stderr through the ProcessSupervisor so output is captured by the bounded-output sinks (BoundedOutputReceipt). The bounded output receipts keep each attempt's output isolated: the rival attempt's stdout/stderr paths are not affected, and the flood does not corrupt the shared state store.
assertions: The flooding worker's stdout/stderr are captured by the BoundedOutputSink (BoundedOutputReceipt with streamDigest, artifactDigest, originalBytes, storedBytes, truncated, tailBase64) through the AttemptRunner's dispatch authority (the production supervised-output path)
The stored bytes are bounded by the output limit (storedBytes <= outputLimitBytes); the flood is truncated when originalBytes exceeds the output limit

The supervision result's outcome is checked: an unsuccessful supervision result (nonzero exit, timeout, spawn error) fails closed and is NOT accepted as success (supervisionSuccessful=true requires outcome=exited and exitCode=0)
The dispatch authority is exercised (dispatchAuthorityExercised=true); the output-flood routes through the AttemptRunner's dispatch authority, not a direct ProcessSupervisor.run() call
The rival attempt's stdout path is not mutated by the flood
The rival attempt's stderr path is not mutated by the flood
The shared state store is not corrupted by the output flood (PRAGMA quick_check returns ok; PRAGMA foreign_key_check reports zero violations)
